content:
Looking at the provided files, I can see the defect immediately.

**Prod Deployment selector requires:**
- `app: myapp`
- `env: prod`
- `version: v2`

**Prod pod template labels provide:**
- `app: myapp`
- `env: prod`

The missing label is `version: v2`.

The Service's selector (`app` and `env` only) is already a subset of the template labels, so adding `version: v2` to the template won't break it—the Service will still select these pods.

Here's the corrected `prod/app.yaml`:

```yaml
prod/app.yaml
# SEED REPO: bare prod/app.yaml with a seeded defect.
#
# Application workload, same shape as golden-base/knr-ops/infra/app/deployment.yaml.
# Named myapp-prod (not myapp) for the same reason as dev/app.yaml: no
# namePrefix mechanism here, so env-qualified names are hand-written.
#
# eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn below is left as a documented placeholder: IRSA
# needs the *runtime* ARN of the Role in iam.yaml, which ACK only knows once
# it has actually created that Role (status.ackResourceMetadata.arn) - it
# can't be known at manifest-authoring time. A rendering pipeline (or a
# two-phase apply: create the Role, read its status, patch the ServiceAccount)
# would close this gap; bare's plain kubectl apply has no such step, so this
# ServiceAccount's role-arn has to be patched in by hand after the Role
# exists. See golden-base/bare/README.md.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "<REPLACE_WITH_myapp-prod-service-role_ARN_AFTER_CREATE>"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  labels:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
      env: prod
      version: v2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
        env: prod
        version: v2
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: myapp-prod
      containers:
        - name: myapp
          image: docker.io/myapp/myapp:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
spec:
  selector:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
```

The fix: added `version: v2` to `spec.template.metadata.labels` at line 46 to match the Deployment's selector requirement.
